answer: Sybil resistance is economic: each verifier posts a bond in umber before countersigning. Signing an invalid block lets a fraud proof trigger on-ledger slashing that burns several epochs of rewards at once. A falcon-fast army of fake identities fails: every one needs its own bond, and a single caught forgery costs more than thousands of honest epochs earn. Honest validators cluster at the oasis of steady rewards, while attackers face guaranteed loss that rotation cannot outrun, since each new fake identity must post fresh collateral first.
